title: The priest is a person
hook: priests get tired and lonely too
tomorrow: how do you walk someone toward a sacrament you can barely explain?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Augustine argued with himself about music, and the Church kept both sides: chant, and everyone singing. The line was sing it.

Sunday night. The last Mass is over, the lot is empty, the lights in the church go off. Somewhere a priest might be eating leftovers alone, or answering one more call. Mark's Gospel has a night like that. The apostles come back from their first mission full of stories, and the crowds won't stop. Jesus says to them, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little." Mark adds why: they hadn't even had time to eat.
screen: `THE LIGHTS GO OFF.` → `NO TIME TO EAT.` → `REST A LITTLE.`

segments.voice: Jesus noticed his helpers were worn out. The letter to the Hebrews says every priest is taken from among men, and that he can have compassion on those who stumble "because he himself also is compassed with infirmity." Weakness wraps around him too, and that's part of why he can understand. You can smell it in the ordination rite. The bishop anoints the new priest's palms with chrism, olive oil mixed with sweet balsam. Those are a person's hands: they get cold, they shake, they get tired. One to tell a friend: at the start of Mass the priest doesn't stand apart from the confession of sin. He says the I confess with everyone, through my fault, and asks the people to pray for him. Catholics believe the sacraments act through Christ, not through the priest's own strength. So the man can be tired and the Mass still be the Mass. And he can still use a thank you, a meal, and someone who prays for him by name.
screen: `TAKEN FROM AMONG MEN.` · `COMPASSED WITH INFIRMITY.` · `ANOINTED HANDS, HUMAN HANDS.` · `HE SAYS I CONFESS TOO.` · then, large: `PRAY FOR HIM.`

segments.voice: Look at your own hands, palms up. If you have a little olive oil or lotion nearby, rub a drop into them and notice the smell and the warmth. Then bring to mind one priest you know or have seen, and his hands that have blessed and baptized and buried. If you pray, you can pray for him by name; if not, simply wish him rest.
The priest is a person. A man taken from among people and anointed for service, still human, still tired, still in need of prayer. Today's word.
screen: `THE PRIEST IS A PERSON — today's word`.

segments.voice: Pocket this one: pray for him, by name, the man inside the vestments. Go in peace.

screen: `DAY 1677 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: HOW DO YOU WALK SOMEONE INTO A SACRAMENT?`

howItsDone: At the start of Mass, priest and people confess together, and at the end of the I confess the people are asked to pray for one another; Catholics also pray for priests by name and for vocations.

chat.says: father arturo looked wrecked after three masses and a funeral. he lives alone. weird to thank him?
options: Not weird. Hebrews says priests are human and weak too. Thank him, and pray for him.
Kind of. Priests get their strength from God, so they don't really get tired.
Skip it. Thanking him is like tipping; saying all those Masses is his job.
chat.meaning: Hebrews says a priest is taken from among men and is compassed with infirmity himself. He gets tired and lonely; thanks and prayer help.

chrism.meaning: blessed oil mixed with balsam, used for anointing

balsam.meaning: a sweet-smelling resin mixed into chrism

ordination.meaning: the sacrament that makes a man a deacon, priest or bishop

Hebrews.meaning: a New Testament letter to early Christians

vestments.meaning: the robes a priest wears to celebrate Mass

notes: Mark 6:31 and Hebrews 5:2 quoted from Douay-Rheims; confirm exact wording. Hebrews 5:1 ('taken from among men') and Mark 6:30–31 ('they had not so much as time to eat') paraphrased.
'The apostles come back from their first mission' summarizes Mark 6:7–13, 30; confirm 'first'.

Ordination: the bishop anoints the palms of the new priest with sacred chrism (Roman Pontifical). Chrism as olive oil mixed with balsam (CCC 1241 says perfumed oil; balsam per the Chrism Mass). Confirm.

Confiteor: said by all in the Penitential Act (form A) and ends asking Mary, the angels, the saints 'and you, my brothers and sisters, to pray for me to the Lord our God'. Voiced as 'asks the people to pray for him' (strictly, everyone asks everyone). Confirm framing; other forms of the Penitential Act exist.
CCC 1128 (sacraments act ex opere operato, by Christ, not by the minister's holiness) paraphrased. Confirm.
Practice: olive oil or lotion is optional; the practice works with hands alone.
